findings.reason: locking the recommendation as written leaves the render step's owner and output path unnamed, so the node dispatched to §4 would build the selection rule without the conversion the decision requires.
findings.text: the `svg-figure-delivery` decision is bound by `data-sections="s4,s8"` and recommends `render-to-png` ("the dispatch renders each SVG figure to PNG … and attaches the PNG"), but no section of the plan carries that render: §3's format-boundary paragraph (lines 176–180) poses it as a question whose answer "is either a render-to-PNG step in the figure contract or a scoped claim that only PNG figures are reviewable", §8 is declared done and only measured SVG reaching nothing, and §4 (deferred) states selection-by-artifact, sequencing, review separation and the caption rule, with no mention of rendering; so once the lead locks the recommended option, the only section named to act on it has no measure producing it, and the two declared setters of `TaskNode.images` (§6's `crew dispatch --image` and §4's figure review) name no producer of the PNG that gets attached

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/_backends.py:1220` is the codex `argv()` composer (line 1223 builds `[command, "exec", "--json", "-i", …]`); `declared_input_modalities` (`reckon/flight.py:1742`), `missing_input_modalities` (1757) and `select_profile_backend` (1769) all exist; `docs/state/reckon/flight.yaml` carries the codex `input_modalities: [text, image]` declaration; the three `plan-commits` shas (f2ea9301, 5b1759ab, 428477c7) all resolve; `docs/figures/` exists; the two decision `data-key`s match the followups that name them.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each landed section carries a measurable gate with a declared negative control (`§1` fall-through mutation, `§2`/`§6` dropped-`-i` mutation, `§7` prompt-described figure, `§8` image-withheld controls), and the one implementable section `§9` declares both its test file and a control that removes the `input_modalities` line from a scratch copy of the layer. §9's control fails the test it guards, so it is a real control rather than an assertion that holds however the code behaves.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate evidence lands under the run's report directory; the cited durable artifacts exist in the repository: `docs/evidence/archive/a-review-can-see-the-figure-landed.html` carries `#s1-input-modalities`, `#s2-attachment-reaching-argv`, `#s6-dispatch-carries-figures`, `#s7-codex-declares-image-input`, `#s8-codex-judges-five-png-pairs`, and `docs/figures/a-review-can-see-the-figure/attachment-reaches-argv.svg` exists. `§9` writes only `tests/test_codex_declares_image_input.py` and reads nothing outside the repository and a temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the decision keys `svg-figure-delivery` and `figure-review-on-metered-lane` are config identifiers, the changed context carries no ticket number, version tag or plan label, and the plain-text rewrite removes markup rather than adding any.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the two contexts themselves are correct and the escaped-markup defect the earlier review raised is properly fixed (the surface extracts `.r-dec-ctx` with `_txt` at `reckon/_plan_html.py:1281` and renders it as a React text child at `docs/ui/decision.jsx:46`, so plain text is the right form, and no surface renders that field as inner HTML), but the `svg-figure-delivery` decision asserts a landing place whose sections carry no mechanism for its recommended option.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §6 is the one place worth checking (it spans `TaskNode.images`, the `crew dispatch --image` CLI, and the resume and lane-change call sites), but all four are one deliverable — a node's figures reach the launcher on every path — measured by one gate; §7 measures delivery for one lane, §8 the five pairs, §9 the declaration.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan declares `plan-informs: scoring-should-stop-a-promotion`, and the divergence the earlier review raised there (that plan's §6 naming `select_profile_backend` as its first dispatch caller, which §4 retires) is disclosed in this plan's own `c-s4-scoring-plan-caller` comment, which names the plan's §6 as a dependency of §4's rewrite; the section declarations (`s1,s2,s5,s6,s7,s8` done; `s3,s4` deferred; `s9` implementable) agree with each section's `data-status`.
